# Where Asía works now: the myths behind the markets
Every age hires the same gods; only the job titles change. **Asía** never stopped working.

In Greek myth Asía is both a divine woman and the continental body that bears her name. As the daughter of Oceanus and Tethys, she belongs to the oldest generation of Greek genealogy, yet her fame rests on her union with the Titan Prometheus, the forethinker who gave fire to mortals. Through her, the eastern continent becomes more than geography: it is the land touched by Prometheus's gift and the threshold from which Asia's civilizations enter the Greek imagination. Asia Minor and the wider continent inherited the name through Persian satrapies and Greek colonies. The Roman province of Asia formalized the term, while medieval and modern usage divided the landmass into Near, Middle, and Far East. Today the name Asia denotes the largest continent, yet its Greek mythic origin in a figure pursued across the sea still echoes in every map.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **4 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## The Myth at Work

**Asia, Bride of Prometheus.** Hesiod names Asia among the Oceanids, the daughters of Oceanus and Tethys (Theogony 357–362).  The eponymy that makes her the wife of the Titan Prometheus belongs to Herodotus (4. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

**The Continent That Took Her Name.** Ancient Greeks explained the name of Asia through the woman.  Herodotus, writing in the fifth century BCE, records the view that the continent was named for Prometheus's wife Asia, just as Europe was named for Europa and Libya for the daughter of Epaphus. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

*A continent’s name; place branding at planetary scale.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Asía performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Mapping & Geospatial

*Maps, GIS, and location intelligence. (Sector: Technology & Innovation)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *A continent's name fixed by the Roman province; every map repeats her.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Ancestry & Heritage Services

*Genealogy, heritage research, and DNA ancestry. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*Wife of Prometheus and mother of Deucalion; the eponymous ancestress of the East.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Asía performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Textiles, Weaving & Networks

*Fabric, fashion textiles, and woven structure. (Sector: Home & Lifestyle)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The Loom of Asía; her own genealogy ties the continent to weaving.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: In Greek myth Asía is both a divine woman and the continental body that bears her name. The age changed. The work did not.
